transcript.text: Hi, I've got a Dyson V15 Detect (SV22) about 4 months old. When I go from the kitchen tiles onto the lounge rug the motor suddenly gets much louder and the battery number drops faster, then it calms down again when I go back on the tiles. Also the screen goes up and down by itself. Is the motor on its way out? It's still under guarantee so I want to report it before it dies completely.

It does not sound like a motor that is about to fail. A motor fault would normally stay noisy regardless of floor type, often with a rough grinding, screeching or harsh whine. The V15 Detect can automatically increase suction when it meets a rug or detects more dust. That makes the motor noticeably louder and uses the battery faster; the on-screen display/power bar changing at the same time is consistent with that adjustment. Calming down again on tiles strongly supports normal operation. 1. Check which power mode is selected. If it is in Auto mode, try Eco or a fixed lower setting for a minute on the rug. A reduced noise and slower battery drop would confirm it is responding normally to the surface/load.
2. With the vacuum switched off, turn the floorhead over and remove any hair or thread around the brush bar. Also check the wand and bin inlet for a partial blockage. A restriction can make a vacuum work harder, although it would usually affect it on all floors rather than only the rug.
3. Make sure the filter is clean, correctly fitted and fully dry if it has been washed. A dirty or damp filter can increase noise and battery use. If the noise becomes rough, metallic, grinding or persists equally on hard floor with a clear, clean airway, report it under the guarantee. At four months old, I would use Dyson support rather than dismantling or attempting a repair. On the pattern described alone, though, this is much more likely to be the vacuum adapting to the rug than a failing motor.

I checked, and the screen says 'Auto'. In Eco it stays the same quiet sound on the rug and the tiles, and in Boost it's loud all the time. The brush bar is clean, the wand is clear, and I washed the filter last month and let it dry for a day. There's no burning smell, heat or sparks, and no warning lights. So is Auto doing this normally?

Yes — that pattern is normal for Auto mode, not a sign that the motor is failing. Your Eco and Boost tests are the useful confirmation: Eco holds a steady quiet power level, Boost holds a steady loud one, while Auto varies the power according to the floor/load it detects. A rug creates more resistance and can contain more fine dust, so Auto can increase suction; that makes it louder and shortens the displayed battery runtime. Returning to quiet operation on tiles is exactly what would be expected. The screen changing at the same time can also be normal: depending on which display is selected, it may update the estimated run time as power changes or show changing dust information. I would not report this as a developing motor fault on the evidence so far. Use the guarantee if it starts making a rough grinding, screeching or irregular noise in Eco as well as Auto, stays loud on hard floors with a clear airway, loses suction, cuts out, overheats, or shows a warning message.
